description: ocsp.rs: the OcspChecker struct-level doc (line 59) mentions that if no SingleResponse matches the serial number, OcspStatusUnknown is returned. However the RevocationChecker::check_revocation doc on the trait (lib.rs lines 194-216) does not list OcspStatusUnknown as a possible error and its description of Ok(()) does not mention the 'not covered by this OCSP response' case. Unlike CRL, the OCSP checker does NOT return Ok(()) for unmatched serials — it hard-fails with OcspStatusUnknown. This asymmetry is not called out in the trait doc, leaving callers to discover it from the struct-level doc or source. Suggested fix: add to the OcspChecker impl's check_revocation doc (or the struct doc) an explicit note that this checker always hard-fails on unmatched serials, contrasting it with CrlChecker's Ok(())-for-unknown behavior.
title: P3: OcspChecker doc: 'SingleResponse not found → OcspStatusUnknown' not documented on check_revocation
